In the latest generic congressional voting poll by Economist/YouGov, 40% said if elections for Congress were being held today, they'd vote for the Democratic candidate compared to 32% that said Republican. A whopping 29% said other, not sure or that they would not vote at all.

In Polymarket betting odds on who will win the 2026 midterms, the odds are now favoring a Democratic Party win in both the Senate and the House.

results.content:
## Polling averages update

All numbers are as of 1:00 PM Eastern on Aug. 6, 2026.

### 2026 U.S. House generic ballot

The Democratic margin in the 2026 U.S. House generic ballot grew this week, rounding to 7 points. The average number of likely voters saying they plan to vote for a Republican fell from 43.5 percent on July 31 to 42.5 percent today, a full point, while the number who say they plan to vote for a Democrat fell less than half a percent, from 49.4 to 49.0.
results.title: Affordability concerns are even more important to voters than in 2024

results.content:
Among registered voters, Democrats led the generic congressional ballot 42 percent to 37 percent. Independents favored Democratic candidates by 12 points.

Reuters/Ipsos surveyed 4,505 U.S. adults nationwide online July 30-August 3. The poll had a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

## Competitive Districts Show Similar Pattern

New analysis from Economist/YouGov suggested Democratic strength extends beyond heavily blue districts.
